title: The kernel workbench's starter matmul: BF16, or E4M3 with row and column scales, FP32 out, one warp an output row

matmul.what: y[columns][N] = x[columns][K] . w[N][K]^T on CUDA cores: one warp an output row with every column (up to 16), each lane a strided share of K, FP32 sums in a fixed order and one xor-shuffle tree; a correct starting point a workbench copies, nothing to tune
